summary: Created a five-phase, four-wave implementation plan for Gate 8's expected-versus-new failure distinction. The design is consumer-side only: pass run-all.sh's existing --fail-on-new flag and branch three ways (pass / warn_advisory / fail), requiring zero code change to tests/run-all.sh or lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh. The plan states the chosen semantics explicitly (an all-expected run exits zero but stays distinguishable via a [WARN] narrative, a WARN-FINDING line invisible to deploy_findings_snapshot's '^FINDING ' filter, and a GATE_DIRTY_LIST cache-invalidation append) and justifies it against six consumers, two of which the dispatch did not name.

artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan: Gate 8 three-way branch; fixture suite with four cases plus non-vacuousness probes; consumer re-verification and the baseline-skew answer; documentation convergence; redeploy and full gate set.
